title: Higher Order OTOCs in Chaotic Quantum Maps: Ruelle-Pollicott Resonances and Asymptotic Freeness
authors: Nicolás Gómez Brucks, Ignacio García-Mata, Diego A. Wisniacki
abstract: Out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) measure the scrambling of information and are a powerful diagnostic of chaos. In chaotic quantum systems with a classical analog, their relaxation towards equilibrium is dictated by the classical Ruelle--Pollicott resonances. We investigate higher-order OTOCs in quantum maps, prototypical one-body systems with a classical limit showing all the essential features of chaotic dynamics. We demonstrate numerically that in the intermediate-time regime they decay exponentially at a rate that depends only on the parity of the order: odd-order OTOCs decay at the same rate as classical correlations, given by the leading Ruelle--Pollicott resonance, and even-order ones at twice that rate. Both are far slower than the naive expectation, under which the rate would grow in proportion to the order. We then mimic the effect of an environment by defining a coarse-grained superoperator whose effect is to introduce decoherence into the system, and find that the expected proportionality between rate and order is thereby restored. Finally, we show that at long times each higher-order OTOC becomes dominated by a single free cumulant, whose saturation value falls off inversely with the dimension of the Hilbert space, signalling the emergence of asymptotic freeness and highlighting the relevance of free probability theory as a framework for the study of quantum chaos.
summary: This paper analyzes higher-order OTOCs in chaotic quantum maps to study information scrambling. It finds that the decay rates are governed by the parity of the order, and that the system eventually reaches a state of asymptotic freeness. This work highlights the utility of free probability theory in characterizing quantum chaos dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates higher-order Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators (OTOCs) to diagnose information scrambling and chaos in quantum systems.
main_result: The decay rates of $k$-OTOCs in the intermediate-time regime depend only on the parity of the order, and at long times, the system exhibits asymptotic freeness characterized by free cumulants.
method: The analysis uses numerical investigation of $k$-OTOCs, comparing unitary evolution with coarse-grained evolution simulating decoherence, and employing free probability theory.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum maps (like the Standard Map or Harper Map) defined on the torus, which serve as prototypical one-body systems with a well-defined classical chaotic limit.
key_observables: Higher-order OTOCs ($k$-OTOCs), free cumulants ($\kappa_{2k}$), and the leading Ruelle-Pollicott resonance ($\lambda_1$).
important_parameters: Intermediate time regime, long time limit, parity of the order $k$, and the coarse-graining parameter $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the system dynamics can be effectively described by the leading Ruelle-Pollicott resonances in the classical limit, and that the coarse-graining procedure correctly models environmental decoherence.
figures_summary: Figures show exponential decay of even-order OTOCs related to the leading resonance, and plots confirm the scaling of free cumulant saturation values inversely with the Hilbert space dimension ($d^{-1}$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by introducing OTOCs and quantum maps, analyzing the intermediate-time decay rates relative to classical resonances, then introducing decoherence to restore expected scaling, and finally demonstrating the emergence of asymptotic freeness via free cumulants at long times.
why_interesting: The connection between quantum chaos diagnostics (OTOCs) and the mathematical framework of free probability theory, particularly the emergence of freeness, provides deep insights into the thermalization and scrambling dynamics of quantum many-body systems.
